original_question: Did Beard and Shoma Morita advocate the same treatment for people with neurasthenia?

final_qi.question: Did Beard advocate the same treatment for people with neurasthenia as Shoma Morita?
final_qi.long_answer:
George Miller Beard (1839-1883), the American neurologist who popularised the diagnosis of neurasthenia, recommended such measures as general rest, travel, nutritious diet, tonics and—above all—systematic electrical stimulation ("electro-therapeutics") to restore the allegedly exhausted nervous system.  

Shōma Morita (1874-1938), the Japanese psychiatrist who developed what is now called Morita therapy, treated neurasthenic and anxiety-type patients with a very different method: an initial period of strict bed-rest and isolation, followed by progressively graded outdoor/occupational activity and psychotherapeutic guidance aimed at accepting unwanted feelings while engaging in purposeful action.  

Because Beard’s principal therapeutic strategy centred on electrical treatment and somatic tonics, whereas Morita’s centred on structured rest, behavioural exposure and acceptance-based psychotherapy, their treatments are not the same. Hence, Beard did not advocate the same treatment for neurasthenia as Shōma Morita.
